ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7) and remind the driver that cancellation fees are only valid where the driver has reached the pickup point, per Ryde's arrival rules.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the chat (F7, F8) and the driver's statement (F10) contain no threat, harassment, abuse or dangerous-driving allegation; dispute type is no_show, not safety. safety_concern = none.

Service type is RydeX (non-taxi), cancelled_by = rider, so NS-0 routes the fee to NS-4. Accepted 17:12:00, rider cancelled 17:15:05 — 3 min 5 s after matching [F2], i.e. beyond the 3-minute grace window, so the $6.61 fee [F5] is prima facie chargeable under NS-4. Ryde has no published "driver later than ETA → free cancellation" rule (NS-8, informative only; no ETA fact here), so the rider's lateness argument cannot by itself waive the fee.

However, the record shows the driver never arrived: the closest approach was 1725 m [F1], driver_arrived_at is null [F3], and no arrival confirmation exists — no "I'm Here" tap and no platform auto-arrival [F4]. The driver's statement [F10] is a claim, not consent or an arrival record, and system records (timeline/GPS) override statements. Ryde's stated basis for charging is arrival at the pickup point; on this record the arrival element is not evidenced. On the plain application of the fee's precondition (no arrival confirmation, driver >1.7 km away, F3/F4/F1), the fee is not collectable.

Amount: only the disputed $6.61 cancellation fee [F5] is refunded in full; no surge applies [F6], and traffic/weather facts (F11–F13) do not affect this fee.

No flag_account: NS-2's flag applies where the driver tapped "I'm Here" outside the pickup radius — here the driver never tapped at all [F4], and the driver's profile shows 0 upheld disputes [F15], so no clause calls for an account flag. Cancel-rate/account action is Ryde's own mechanism (NS-3), not part of this ruling.

rejected_claims.reason: Ryde has no rule granting free cancellation when the driver is late relative to ETA (NS-8 is informative only, not citable); the rider's complaint of lateness alone does not waive the fee. The refund rests instead on the absent arrival confirmation (F3, F4) and the 1725 m closest approach (F1).

Driver's post-hoc statement that the rider cancelled while he was on the way (F10) is not supported by any arrival record (F3, F4) and system records override statements; it also cannot establish the NS-1 arrival elements.
